quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hungarian is one of the few languages in Europe that isn't part of the Indo-European language family—it's related to Finnish and Estonian instead! The Hungarian word 'virág' (meaning flower) sounds almost musical, and Hungary is famous for its beautiful gardens and love of flowers.

short_read.title: Harbor Seals of the Pacific Northwest
short_read.teaser: These playful marine mammals are common visitors to the Strait of Juan de Fuca, often seen lounging on rocks or popping their heads up curiously. Learn about their fascinating behaviors and how they've adapted to life in the Salish Sea.

medium_read.title: The Secret Lives of Hummingbirds
medium_read.teaser: These tiny jewels of the garden have hearts that beat over 1,200 times per minute and can remember every flower they've visited. Discover the amazing world of hummingbirds and how to welcome them to your garden.

long_read.title: The Story of Budapest's Thermal Baths
long_read.teaser: For over 2,000 years, Hungarians have cherished their thermal bath culture, from Roman times through Ottoman rule to today's grand bathhouses. This journey through history explores how these healing waters became such an important part of Hungarian life and culture.

port_angeles.title: Black-tailed Deer Season at Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: Late August is a beautiful time to spot Olympic black-tailed deer at Hurricane Ridge, especially in the early morning hours. These graceful animals are often seen grazing in the meadows, and their fawns are still sporting their spots this time of year!

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's wings can beat up to ___ times per second!
puzzle_1.correct_response: That's right! Incredible, isn't it? Those tiny wings move so fast they create that lovely humming sound we hear.
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! The answer is 80 beats per second—almost too fast for our eyes to see!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those tiny wings actually beat about 80 times per second! That's why they make that distinctive humming sound.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: A hummingbird's rapid wing beats allow them to hover in place and even fly backwards—the only birds that can do this! Their wing muscles make up about 30% of their total body weight.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful! Pillangó is such a pretty word for such a pretty creature, isn't it?
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó'—doesn't it sound lovely? (Virág means flower, madár means bird, and napsugár means sunshine.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungary is home to over 200 species of butterflies, including the beautiful Swallowtail. Hungarian gardens have long celebrated these delicate visitors with flower plantings designed to attract them.

puzzle_3.question: What tree produces the acorns that are a favorite food of squirrels and deer?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Yes! Oak trees produce acorns, and they're absolutely vital for wildlife on the Olympic Peninsula and beyond. A single oak can produce thousands of acorns in a good year!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's the oak tree! These magnificent trees produce acorns that feed everything from squirrels and deer to jays and woodpeckers. They're true pillars of the forest ecosystem.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Oak trees can live for hundreds of years, and some of the oaks in Olympic National Forest are over 300 years old. Native Americans traditionally ground acorns into flour for cooking.
